newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB sells 2,000 tonnes of wheat in tender 25.
newsitem.headline: AWB sells 2,000 tonnes of wheat in tender 25.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Wednesday it sold 2,000 tonnes of Australian Premium White (APW) wheat at A$210.00 a tonne in its latest tender for sales from its national pool.
Total bids were received for 36,000 tonnes of current crop wheat and for 18,000 tonnes of 1997/98 new season wheat, it said.
The successful APW sale was for 1996/97 current crop wheat.
AWB said its reserve price for Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat was A$204 a tonne, Newcastle delivery, for current crop wheat and A$195 for new season wheat.
The highest failed bids for Newcastle ASW were A$190 a tonne for the current crop and A$173 for new crop wheat.
The successful bid for 2,000 tonnes of APW was for Port Adelaide delivery.

The next tender would be held on June 25, AWB said.
Note: ASW = Australian Standard White; ASWN = ASW noodle wheat; APH = Australian Prime Hard; AH1 = Australian Hard 1; APW = Australian Premium White.
